intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that retinitis pigmentosa-56 (RP56) is caused by homozygous mutation in the IMPG2 gene (607056) on chromosome 3.

checks.claim: Retinitis pigmentosa-56 (RP56) is caused by homozygous mutation in the IMPG2 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Sequence analysis of IMPG2 in the two index cases revealed homozygous mutations cosegregating with the disease in the respective families
checks.explanation: The paper reports homozygous IMPG2 mutations causing autosomal-recessive RP. The RP56 designation is OMIM nomenclature and is not in the abstract.

checks.claim: The IMPG2 gene is located on chromosome 3.
checks.evidence_quote: sharing large overlapping homozygous regions that harbored the IMPG2 gene on chromosome 3
checks.explanation: The abstract states directly that IMPG2 is on chromosome 3.

paragraphs.text: Retinitis pigmentosa-56 (RP56) is an autosomal recessive form of retinitis pigmentosa (Bandah-Rozenfeld et al., 2010). Retinitis pigmentosa is a heterogeneous group of inherited retinal diseases caused by progressive degeneration of the photoreceptor cells. Patients have progressive visual-field loss (Bandah-Rozenfeld et al., 2010).

checks.claim: Retinitis pigmentosa-56 (RP56) is an autosomal recessive form of retinitis pigmentosa.
checks.evidence_quote: Mutations in IMPG2, encoding interphotoreceptor matrix proteoglycan 2, cause autosomal-recessive retinitis pigmentosa.
checks.explanation: The title states that IMPG2-related RP is autosomal recessive.

checks.claim: Retinitis pigmentosa is a heterogeneous group of inherited retinal diseases.
checks.evidence_quote: Retinitis pigmentosa (RP) is a heterogeneous group of inherited retinal diseases caused by progressive degeneration of the photoreceptor cells.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Retinitis pigmentosa is caused by progressive degeneration of the photoreceptor cells.
checks.evidence_quote: Retinitis pigmentosa (RP) is a heterogeneous group of inherited retinal diseases caused by progressive degeneration of the photoreceptor cells.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Patients with retinitis pigmentosa-56 have progressive visual-field loss.
checks.evidence_quote: Most patients with IMPG2 mutations showed an early-onset form of RP with progressive visual-field loss and deterioration of visual acuity.
checks.explanation: The paper says 'most' patients, not all. The patient with the missense mutation had maculopathy instead.

paragraphs.text: Bandah-Rozenfeld et al. (2010) studied 2 families with autosomal recessive retinitis pigmentosa, each with 3 affected sibs. Most patients with IMPG2 mutations had progressive visual-field loss. The patient with the missense mutation was diagnosed with maculopathy rather than retinitis pigmentosa.

checks.claim: Bandah-Rozenfeld et al. (2010) studied 2 families with autosomal recessive retinitis pigmentosa.
checks.evidence_quote: Using autozygosity mapping, we identified two families, each with three affected siblings sharing large overlapping homozygous regions that harbored the IMPG2 gene on chromosome 3.
checks.explanation: Two families are stated, and the disease is arRP.

checks.claim: Each of the 2 families with autosomal recessive retinitis pigmentosa studied by Bandah-Rozenfeld et al. (2010) had 3 affected sibs.
checks.evidence_quote: we identified two families, each with three affected siblings
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Most patients with IMPG2 mutations studied by Bandah-Rozenfeld et al. (2010) had progressive visual-field loss.
checks.evidence_quote: Most patients with IMPG2 mutations showed an early-onset form of RP with progressive visual-field loss and deterioration of visual acuity.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: The patient with an IMPG2 missense mutation studied by Bandah-Rozenfeld et al. (2010) was diagnosed with maculopathy rather than retinitis pigmentosa.
checks.evidence_quote: The patient with the missense mutation, however, was diagnosed with maculopathy.
checks.explanation: The word 'however' sets this diagnosis against RP.

paragraphs.text: The transmission pattern of RP56 in the families reported by Bandah-Rozenfeld et al. (2010) was consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.

checks.claim: The transmission pattern of RP56 in the families reported by Bandah-Rozenfeld et al. (2010) was consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.
checks.evidence_quote: revealed homozygous mutations cosegregating with the disease in the respective families
checks.explanation: Homozygous mutations that cosegregate in sibships with arRP fit autosomal recessive inheritance.

paragraphs.text: Bandah-Rozenfeld et al. (2010) used homozygosity (autozygosity) mapping in families with autosomal recessive retinitis pigmentosa and identified a homozygous region on chromosome 3q that contained the IMPG2 gene.

checks.claim: Bandah-Rozenfeld et al. (2010) used homozygosity (autozygosity) mapping in families with autosomal recessive retinitis pigmentosa.
checks.evidence_quote: Using autozygosity mapping, we identified two families, each with three affected siblings
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Bandah-Rozenfeld et al. (2010) identified a homozygous region on chromosome 3q that contained the IMPG2 gene in families with autosomal recessive retinitis pigmentosa.
checks.evidence_quote: sharing large overlapping homozygous regions that harbored the IMPG2 gene on chromosome 3
checks.explanation: The abstract says chromosome 3. The 'q' arm is standard location wording for IMPG2.

paragraphs.text: Meunier et al. (2014) reported a heterozygous mutation in the IMPG2 gene in a family with vitelliform macular dystrophy with autosomal dominant transmission.

checks.claim: Meunier et al. (2014) reported a heterozygous mutation in the IMPG2 gene in a family with vitelliform macular dystrophy.
checks.evidence_quote: With an autosomal dominant transmission, families 1 and 2 had the c.713T→G (p.Leu238Arg) mutation in IMPG1 and family 4 had the c.3230G→T (p.Cys1077Phe) mutation in IMPG2.
checks.explanation: The abstract reports an IMPG2 mutation (p.Cys1077Phe) in one family with vitelliform macular dystrophy. It does not use the word 'heterozygous', but the mutation segregates dominantly, which implies a heterozygous state.

checks.claim: The vitelliform macular dystrophy in the family with a heterozygous IMPG2 mutation reported by Meunier et al. (2014) showed autosomal dominant transmission.
checks.evidence_quote: With an autosomal dominant transmission, families 1 and 2 had the c.713T→G (p.Leu238Arg) mutation in IMPG1 and family 4 had the c.3230G→T (p.Cys1077Phe) mutation in IMPG2.
checks.explanation: The abstract states autosomal dominant transmission for family 4, the family with the IMPG2 mutation.

paragraphs.text: In affected members of families with autosomal recessive retinitis pigmentosa, Bandah-Rozenfeld et al. (2010) found homozygous mutations in the IMPG2 gene, which encodes interphotoreceptor matrix proteoglycan-2, a constituent of the interphotoreceptor matrix. The mutations cosegregated with the disease in the families. Most of the mutations were nonsense mutations predicted to truncate the protein.

checks.claim: Bandah-Rozenfeld et al. (2010) found homozygous IMPG2 mutations in affected members of families with autosomal recessive retinitis pigmentosa.
checks.evidence_quote: Sequence analysis of IMPG2 in the two index cases revealed homozygous mutations cosegregating with the disease in the respective families
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: The IMPG2 gene encodes interphotoreceptor matrix proteoglycan-2.
checks.evidence_quote: The IMPG2 gene encodes the interphotoreceptor matrix proteoglycan IMPG2, which is a constituent of the interphotoreceptor matrix.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Interphotoreceptor matrix proteoglycan-2 is a constituent of the interphotoreceptor matrix.
checks.evidence_quote: The IMPG2 gene encodes the interphotoreceptor matrix proteoglycan IMPG2, which is a constituent of the interphotoreceptor matrix.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: The IMPG2 mutations identified by Bandah-Rozenfeld et al. (2010) cosegregated with the disease in the families with autosomal recessive retinitis pigmentosa.
checks.evidence_quote: revealed homozygous mutations cosegregating with the disease in the respective families
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Most of the IMPG2 mutations identified by Bandah-Rozenfeld et al. (2010) were nonsense mutations.
checks.evidence_quote: revealed five additional mutations; four nonsense mutations and one missense mutation affecting a highly conserved phenylalanine residue
checks.explanation: Five of the seven mutations are nonsense: one in the Iraqi Jewish family and four in the additional index cases. The other two are a deletion and a missense.

checks.claim: The IMPG2 nonsense mutations identified by Bandah-Rozenfeld et al. (2010) were predicted to truncate the protein.
checks.evidence_quote: four nonsense mutations and one missense mutation affecting a highly conserved phenylalanine residue
checks.explanation: The abstract names nonsense mutations but does not state that they are predicted to truncate the protein. This is implied by the definition of a nonsense mutation, not stated.
